obligation: FSIS notification of adulterated or misbranded product in commerce
trigger: Establishment learns or determines that adulterated or misbranded product received by or originating from it has entered commerce (for example, product shipped while cook, chill, or cold storage CCPs were unmonitored, or after an unexplained setpoint or formulation change, and evaluation finds it adulterated)
deadline: Within 24 hours of learning or determining; include type, amount, origin, and destination of the product
notify: FSIS District Office for each affected plant
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all 8 plants are official establishments
clock_starts: Learning or determining that affected product entered commerce (not discovery of the cyber incident)
owner: Senior Vice President, Food Safety and Quality Assurance

obligation: Reportable Food Registry
trigger: Responsible party (the registrant) determines an article of FDA-regulated food is a reportable food: reasonable probability that its use or exposure will cause serious adverse health consequences or death
deadline: As soon as practicable, and no later than 24 hours after the determination. No report is required if the adulteration originated with the company, was detected before any transfer to another person, and was corrected or the food destroyed (350f(d)(2))
notify: FDA through the Reportable Food Registry electronic portal; also investigate the cause
clock_starts: Determination that the food is a reportable food

obligation: Hazardous substance release to the National Response Center
trigger: Release of anhydrous ammonia at or above 100 lb in any 24-hour period (for example, after a cyber-caused refrigeration upset)
deadline: Immediately on knowledge of the release
owner: Director of Refrigeration and Process Safety

obligation: Emergency release notification to the LEPC and SERC
trigger: Same reportable release
deadline: Immediate notification, then a written follow-up as soon as practicable
notify: Community emergency coordinator for each LEPC likely affected and the SERC of each state likely affected
owner: Director of Refrigeration and Process Safety

obligation: SEC materiality determination
trigger: Any cybersecurity incident that could be material
deadline: Without unreasonable delay after discovery (the disclosure committee convenes within 48 hours under POL-03 4.6)

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 filing
trigger: Incident determined to be material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination

obligation: SEC filing delay on Attorney General determination
trigger: U.S. Attorney General determines that disclosure poses a substantial risk to national security or public safety and notifies the SEC in writing
deadline: Up to 30 days after the original due date; up to 30 more days on a further determination; in extraordinary circumstances a final period of up to 60 days
notify: Request through outside counsel to the Department of Justice
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the Attorney General so determines

obligation: SEC annual cybersecurity disclosure
trigger: Annual report
deadline: With the next Form 10-K; update the description of processes and of any material effects of incidents

obligation: Insider trading blackout
trigger: Disclosure committee convenes on an incident
deadline: Same day the committee convenes
notify: Committee members, responders with knowledge, executives
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - company policy, not a regulatory deadline

obligation: State breach notice to individuals (each state of residence)
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of state residents (definitions vary): employees in 6 states, online store customers nationwide
deadline: Varies by state: some say without unreasonable delay; some set a fixed number of days
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside
clock_starts: Varies by state (often discovery or determination of the breach)

obligation: State attorney general or regulator notice
trigger: Breach above state-set thresholds
deadline: Varies by state

obligation: State consumer reporting agency notice
trigger: Notice to more than a state-set number of residents
deadline: Varies by state
applies_at_this_tier: Yes where the state threshold is met

obligation: State third-party agent (vendor) notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A vendor holding personal information for the company (payroll, ERP, e-commerce) has a breach
deadline: Varies by state; contracts require 10 days

obligation: Florida notice to individuals (worked example)
trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (law enforcement delay and a 15-day extension on good cause provided in writing to the Department within 30 days are available)
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination (the 15-day good-cause extension in 501.171(3)(a) applies only to notice to individuals, not to this notice)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
clock_starts: Decision to notify more than 1,000 individuals

obligation: Florida no-notice determination (worked example)
trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept at least 5 years; provided to the Department within 30 days after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Only if that determination is made

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the company (worked example)
trigger: A vendor maintaining personal information for the company discovers a breach
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after the agent's determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - vendors holding Florida residents' personal information

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (2021-09-21); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransomware payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA

obligation: Law enforcement and CISA report (voluntary)
trigger: Ransomware or other significant cyber incident
deadline: As early as practical (day 0 to day 2 in the runbook)
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary; supports OFAC mitigation and may bring OT response help

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports (PROPOSED - not yet in effect)
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours after reasonable belief a covered cyber incident occurred; 24 hours after a ransom payment is disbursed
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-10-04; as proposed the company would be covered (exceeds the SBA size standard). Recheck when final
clock_starts: Proposed: reasonable belief of a covered incident

obligation: Reporting of cyber incidents at MTSA facilities
trigger: Cyber incident at an MTSA-regulated facility
deadline: Immediately (6.16-1); without delay to the National Response Center for entities not reporting under 6.16-1
notify: FBI, CISA, and the Coast Guard Captain of the Port; or National Response Center

obligation: Covered telecommunications or Kaspersky article discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25 and 52.204-23; FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or a Kaspersky covered article
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - no federal prime contracts or subcontracts; recheck if that changes

obligation: Cyber insurance notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy; call the carrier's breach hotline before engaging vendors

obligation: SL-1 cold storage customer notice
trigger: Incident affecting customer inventory, temperature records, portal data, or deliveries
deadline: Per agreement (standard terms: 24 hours for a service outage or temperature record gap; 10 days for a data breach)

obligation: SL-2 co-manufacturing customer notice
trigger: Incident affecting customer specifications, production record packages, or product safety
deadline: Per agreement (standard terms: 24 hours for a product safety event; 10 days for a data breach)
notify: SL-2 customer quality and security contacts
owner: Vice President, Co-Manufacturing and Private Label

obligation: Retail and foodservice customer notice
trigger: Incident affecting product safety, recalls, or deliveries
deadline: Per each agreement (commonly prompt notice of any recall or food safety event)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual; FSQA keeps the list
owner: Senior Vice President, Food Safety and Quality Assurance
